ai.description: This toad reaches 4–6 cm. It is brown with dark markings and a distinct pale mid-dorsal stripe. It is identified by its exceptionally large parotoid glands and prominent tympanum.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Ingerophrynus macrotis* is best identified by its exceptionally large, vertically elongated tympanum, which is nearly equal in size to its eye.
ai.habitat: *Ingerophrynus macrotis* inhabits moist deciduous forests and scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically found near water bodies at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Big-eared Toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dark to forage for small invertebrates across the forest floor and near temporary water bodies.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ingerophrynus macrotis* breeds in seasonal pools during the monsoon, laying eggs in long, gelatinous strings typical of the genus. Specific clutch sizes remain poorly documented.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Big-eared Toad occurs in Northeast India, primarily within the states of Assam, Meghalaya, and Mizoram, typically inhabiting low-elevation tropical forests.
ai.callDescription: The Big-eared Toad emits a series of high-pitched, rhythmic chirps or trills, typically heard near temporary rain pools and flooded grasslands in lowland forests.
